resources.string: Active samples: %1$d. Evidence covers the last 30 seconds. Several stages can be slow at once; these observations suggest causes, not a guaranteed diagnosis. No video or personal information is recorded.
Not enough recent video to assess. Play for a few seconds with the menu closed, then return just after a stutter.
No repeated bottleneck was observed in the available measurements. Short spikes and unmeasured stages can still cause a stutter.
Network: repeated frame loss or round-trip variation. Try a lower bitrate, a wired host or a less congested Wi-Fi connection.
Decode: output repeatedly took at least one frame interval. Try a lower resolution or frame rate; lowering bitrate alone may not help.
Host: the slower processing samples exceeded the frame interval. Compare game/GPU load and a lower game frame limit. This measurement includes more than encoding.
Presentation: frames were released faster than they were shown, with long display waits. Compare frame-pacing modes and the screen refresh rate.
Temperature: Android reported high thermal pressure. Lower frame rate/resolution or disable expensive client processing; allow the device to cool.

Largest observed values:
Frame loss: %1$s %%
Decode: %2$s ms
Host processing p95: %3$s ms
Display wait p95: %4$s ms
These stages do not add up to input-to-screen latency.

Largest observed values:
Frame loss: %1$s %%
Decode: %2$s ms
Host to network p95: %3$s ms
Display wait p95: %4$s ms
These stages do not add up to input-to-screen latency.
A bitrate trial changes only this session. Compare another 30 seconds of similar gameplay, then return here to undo it. Manual or automatic bitrate changes replace the trial.
The host did not report its current encoder bitrate. The trial was not applied.
The host bitrate has changed since the trial. Undo was cancelled to preserve that change.
The encoder is already at the minimum trial bitrate. No change was made.

Repeating stalls: %2$d network stalls in the last 20 minutes started about every %1$s. A steady rhythm like this usually comes from background Wi-Fi scans on this device or on the PC. To reduce them:
• Android: Settings → Location → Location services, turn off Wi-Fi scanning and Bluetooth scanning.
• Android: leave Developer options → Wi-Fi scan throttling on.
• Close apps that look for networks or nearby devices while streaming.
• PC: connect it by cable, or stop tools that scan for Wi-Fi networks.
Nightjar already holds Android's low-latency Wi-Fi lock while streaming, which asks the system to delay scans; some devices scan anyway.

Bursts: in %1$d of the last %2$d seconds, frames arrived late and then several at once, although the host sent them on time. Something between the host and this device held them back, often Wi-Fi power saving. Try a wired connection, or a 5 or 6 GHz network closer to the router. On a laptop, use mains power or turn off power saving for the Wi-Fi adapter.
